title: John, looking back
hook: the Word, the signs, the vine, and feed my sheep
tomorrow: old people weeping, young people cheering, same moment. where?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Luke: shepherds on the night shift, a rich man up a tree, and a party for a son who came home. Great joy. Today, a Gospel with no manger at all.

Grapes in a grocery store bowl look like they came from nowhere. Somewhere there was a vine, a branch, a long season of staying put. John's Gospel has no manger and no shepherds. It begins before anything was made: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” And on Jesus's last night, it lands on something you could hold in one hand: a branch on a vine.
screen: `GRAPES FROM NOWHERE?` → `IN THE BEGINNING WAS THE WORD.` → `A BRANCH ON A VINE.`

segments.voice: John says plainly why he wrote: “that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.” So he tells signs: water turned to wine at a wedding, a man born blind who sees, Lazarus called out of his tomb. Each one points past itself. Then, on the last night, the picture underneath them: “I am the vine, ye are the branches.” And: “Abide in me, and I in you.” Abide is an old word for stay, remain, make your home. A branch doesn't strain to make grapes. It stays on, and the fruit comes. A detail worth passing on: the book ends with breakfast. A beach, a fire of coals, fish and bread, and Peter, who had denied knowing Jesus on the night of the arrest, is asked, “lovest thou me?” again, and a third time. Each yes is met with a job: feed my sheep. Looking back, John's thread is staying close: the Word who came near, signs that point, branches that stay, and a friend who failed, invited back to stay and to tend.
screen: `SIGNS THAT POINT PAST THEMSELVES.` · `I AM THE VINE.` · `ABIDE: STAY, MAKE YOUR HOME.` · `BREAKFAST ON THE BEACH.` · then, large: `ABIDE IN ME.`

segments.voice: If you have a grape or a raisin, or any fruit, hold it for a moment first: it grew on something that stayed put through a whole season. Then taste it slowly, and notice how long the flavor stays. If you have none, rest your hand on a plant or a wooden table, something that once grew. If you pray, let John's line rest with it: abide in me.
John. The Gospel of the Word, the signs, the vine and its branches, and a breakfast where a friend who failed is sent to feed the sheep.
For the road: abide in me, the branch's whole job. Day seventeen-sixty-eight, and you stayed.

screen: `DAY 1768 COUNTS.` → `THE SUMMIT · 17 OF 40.` → `TOMORROW: WEEPING AND CHEERING, SAME MOMENT. WHERE?`

howItsDone: Some churches read John's opening, In the beginning was the Word, at Christmas, and John's chapters of Jesus' last night, with the vine and the branches, around Holy Week and Easter.

fork.setup: your cousin says he's burned out from trying so hard to be a good Christian. according to John's vine picture, what is a branch's job?

stay connected; the fruit comes from staying.

notes: Written 2026-10-13 in the year-2-4 recipe; rewritten 2026-10-15 in recipe v3 (shape: senses). Title, word and carry kept; John 1:1, 20:31, 15:4–5 and 21 kept. The practice (taste a grape or raisin, or touch a plant) now carries the vine picture.

John 21: the KJV says Jesus asks 'the third time' (21:17); the answer 'feed my lambs' (21:15) then 'feed my sheep' (21:16–17). The fork's reveal quotes the rest of John 15:4 ('as the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine'); confirm wording.
'Abide' glossed as stay, remain, make your home (Greek menō); a meaning, not an etymology. Confirm.
Breakfast detail: John 21:9 has a fire of coals, fish and bread. 'The book ends with breakfast' refers to the last chapter's scene, not the very last verse.
Grace storyline: Grace overpractices the solo until her voice is tired; Pop (her grandfather, the weekly elder) tells her to stop working the song and sit with it.
Original game: Greek μείνατε ἐν ἐμοί (John 15:4). Confirm accents and sound-out.
